label: Grounding among concrete things that come to be after a moment is well-founded
definition: PostAbsenceGroundingWellFounded h Concrete grounds holds when, for every history v and moment s, the relation 'y and x are concrete, each absent at s and present at some moment strictly after s, and grounds v y x' is well-founded: no endless sequence x0, x1, x2, ... of things that all come to be after s, each x(n+1) grounding x(n). An endless past of fathers, each present from his own birth on and grounded by the previous one, satisfies it, because for any s only finitely many of them are absent at s and present later (GroundedBeginnings.Control.beginningless). An endless chain of grounds all coming to be after one empty moment violates it (BegunComingToBe.Control.zeno with predecessor grounds).
note: Analyst formulation; attribution deferred. Exactly what the induction of GroundedBeginnings.nothingFromNothing uses; adopted after the semantic challenge of PR #1478 in place of the stronger PresentGroundingWellFounded, which an endless per accidens past violates. Sense of ground as in the lasting-ground premise (DISAMB-CAUSAL-SERIES): per se and per accidens grounds alike; it excludes an endless series of either kind only when the whole series comes to be after a moment at which all its members are absent. Aquinas's grant that an infinite per accidens series is not impossible (ST I q.46 a.2 ad 7, statement STMT-INFINITE-REGRESS-IMPOSSIBLE-ONLY-IN-PER-SE-SERIES) concerns an eternal past of generations; whether it extends to such a compressed series is an unread, open bridge. Transitivity, asymmetry and irreflexivity are not assumed. Applicability OPEN.
